messages:
Emma: incident-bot just flagged a big 429 spike for multiple enterprise orgs (AcmeCorp, Velox) — dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/ratelimit/429s?panel=overview :eyes:
incident-bot: Alert: 429 rate-limit surge detected — org-level throttles triggered (rule: per_key_burst_override)
Jason: I rolled forward a burst config change from Kartik's PR this morning — was that supposed to be per-key or per-org?
Kartik: It was intended to change the per_key default burst to 1200. I only edited the "burst" value in the unified-rate-schema, didn't plan to modify scope.
Rui: Console shows "Apply to: Organization" in the edit history. @Kartik did you use the Console quick-edit or the API?
Kartik: I used the Console quick-edit. I assumed the scope dropdown preserved "per-key" when editing existing rules, but audit shows it saved scope=org. Here's the audit snippet:
```
PATCH /config/v1/rate-limits/123
payload:
{"scope":"org","rule":"per_key_burst_override","value":1200}
```
Priya: Support seeing a lot of 429s and inbound tickets. Triage ticket #5482. Customers reporting timeouts.
Emma: Can we revert to previous scope and value and then reapply the change scoped to keys only?
Jason: Pushing revert now: `curl -X PATCH https://config.redwood.internal/config/v1/rate-limits/123 -d '{"scope":"key","value":100}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN"`
devops-bot: deploy:config-service: starting rollout of config v2025.11.137 -> 3 nodes
Rui: Reverting helps new tokens, but existing cached routing tables may keep org cap in memory for a bit. We should add an emergency exception for the largest orgs.
Kartik: Creating a temporary exception for AcmeCorp: `allowlist: [{"org":"AcmeCorp","rate":"10r/s"}]` to avoid user-visible errors while revert propagates.
Priya: Support enabling exception now and notifying Acme. Sending templated update to their SRE.
Emma: Filing console bug — the scope dropdown saved the wrong value when editing existing rules. BUG-2127.
Jason: Hotfix plan: 1) revert rule (in progress) 2) add per-org exceptions for impacted customers 3) patch Console to preserve scope on edit + confirm for org-wide edits 4) add e2e to prevent regressions. I'll own 1-2, Kartik owns 3-4.
devops-bot: deploy:config-service: completed on node-1, node-2, node-3 — rollout success
Emma: 429 rate share dropping from ~22% -> 1.5% in the last 10m after revert+exceptions :party-parrot:
Priya: Acme confirmed decreased errors. They'll validate end-to-end and confirm in 30m.
Kartik: Postmortem action items: console UX needs an explicit "scope confirmation" when scope=org is selected, telemetry to differentiate edits-by-console vs API, and stricter guardrails for org-scoped edits.
Jason: Also adding a dashboard alert and runbook step: "Detect sudden scope change affecting >5% of traffic" and require 2FA + approval for scope=org edits.
Emma: Good work. Marking incident mitigated. I'll draft the incident report and link to BUG-2127 + #5482.
devops-bot: incident-bot: Incident mitigated, severity: sev2 -> monitoring
